transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. I'm here because during long meetings or when I'm working through complex plans, my mind keeps drifting off and I miss important details. Even though I'm really trying hard to pay attention, I just can't seem to stay focused.
Did you experience these difficulties with staying focused or staying organized during your childhood, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

While it has become a much bigger problem over the last two years as my responsibilities grew, these issues actually go back to my childhood. Back in elementary school, my teachers always wrote on report cards that I was bright but constantly daydreamed and lost my homework, and my parents used to joke that I'd forget my head if it wasn't attached to my neck.
Besides having trouble focusing, do you often feel restless, like you need to be constantly on the go, or do you frequently interrupt others when they are speaking?

I don't really feel physically restless or driven by a motor, but I absolutely struggle with that second part. When I get excited about a project, I often catch myself talking over people and dominating the conversation with way too much detail. I usually only realize I've been doing it when I notice others checking the clock or not jumping in.
Do you find that you have a hard time remaining seated in situations where you are expected to stay in one place, like at your desk or in a classroom?

No, I don't really have trouble physically staying in my seat. My main issue is that my mind starts wandering or I lose focus while sitting there, rather than feeling a physical need to get up and move around.
Do you often find that you make careless mistakes in your work, or have difficulty keeping track of your belongings or meeting deadlines because of how you manage your time?

Yes, I do. Even with my color-coded spreadsheets, I often skim reports and send them out with miscalculated columns or incorrect date ranges that my team has to point out. I also have to rely on a phone full of half-written reminders just to keep track of tasks, and even then, I still occasionally miss a meeting or a call until someone follows up.

When you are in social or professional settings, do you find that you have a hard time waiting for your turn in conversations or waiting in line, or is your primary difficulty strictly related to sustaining attention on tasks?

My primary and most frustrating struggle is definitely keeping my attention focused on tasks and during meetings. However, I do experience some conversational issues where I catch myself talking over others or dominating discussions when I'm excited about a project, though I don't really have a problem with physical waiting like standing in lines.
